financing_structures.description: Client purchases and owns the system outright. Qualifies fully for Section 12B tax deductions. Preferred by balance-sheet-strong industrials and mining houses with access to corporate finance or green loan facilities.
financing_structures.typical_providers: Absa, Standard Bank, Nedbank, FNB green/sustainability-linked finance at prime+1% to prime+3% over 5â€“7 years.

financing_structures.description: Developer finances, owns, and operates the system on the client's site. Client pays a fixed or escalating R/kWh rate below the Eskom tariff â€” zero upfront capital. Typical contract terms of 10â€“20 years.
financing_structures.typical_providers: SolarAfrica, GreenYellow SA, GreenHouse Capital, Terra Firma, IMPOWER.

financing_structures.description: Client leases the system with a buy-out option at end of term. Monthly payment replaces most of the Eskom bill. Popular in the SME and light-commercial segment.

A large-scale solar plant is built at a remote site; power is delivered to the industrial/mining client via Eskom's Virtual Wheeling programme. No physical installation at the client's site. Preferred for clients with very high demand (>5 MW).
financing_structures.typical_providers: Voltalia, Pele Green Energy, JUWI, SolarAfrica for utility-scale industrial and mining clients.

Poor after-sales service: inverter faults go unresolved for weeks; warranty repairs handed off to third parties with no communication or status updates.

Non-compliance with Certificate of Compliance (CoC) and SSEG registration requirements â€” leaves clients exposed to insurance voidance and grid-connection penalties.
